stepsIntro: You don't need to prepare for everything at once. These five steps will make you and your family significantly better prepared.

steps.text: Stay informed by following the official HM Government of Gibraltar and Royal Gibraltar Police WhatsApp channels — your quickest source of updates before, during and after an incident.

Make a household emergency plan — agree where your family will meet, how you'll stay in contact if phone networks are down, and what route you'd take to safety. Gibraltar is small but emergencies move fast.
Prepare an emergency grab bag with essentials: water, food, torch, battery radio, ID documents, medications, phone charger and cash. Keep it somewhere you can grab it in under a minute.

Know the hazards relevant to Gibraltar — flooding in low-lying areas, summer wildfires on the Upper Rock, extreme heat and power cuts are among the most likely. Read the guidance on this site before an emergency happens.

Check on your neighbours — Gibraltar's close-knit community is one of its greatest strengths. Identify elderly residents, persons with disabilities and people who live alone near you, and agree to look out for each other.

heroSubheadline: Be informed. Make a plan. Be prepared.
heroBody: Emergencies such as flooding, wildfires and power cuts can happen without warning in Gibraltar. Taking a few simple steps now means you and your family will be better prepared when it matters most.
